overview.description: Once your protein is made, you have to extract it - 'there are many ways to skin E. coli'. Lysis releases everything inside the cell as 'cell slurry'; the right enzymes/inhibitors protect your protein of interest during the process.
objectives: choose a lysis method (chemical, sonication, bead-beating)
include protease inhibitors and keep samples cold
clarify lysate to separate soluble protein

instructions.title: Resuspend cold
instructions.description: Resuspend the pellet in cold lysis buffer with protease inhibitors; keep on ice throughout.

instructions.title: Lyse
instructions.description: Sonicate (pulsed, on ice) or bead-beat until the cloudy suspension turns translucent.

instructions.title: Clarify
instructions.description: Centrifuge to separate soluble protein (supernatant) from debris/inclusion bodies (pellet).

submission.description: Lyse an induced culture and keep aliquots of lysate, cleared supernatant and pellet for SDS-PAGE analysis.

kits.name: Lysozyme / lysis reagents
kits.note: Enzymatic/chemical lysis to release protein; keep cold, add protease inhibitors.

kits.name: Ultrasonic homogeniser (budget)
kits.note: Sonicate cells on ice with rest pulses; DNase cuts the viscous lysate.
